plexus-utils is bundled inside the ruby-maven-libs gem, which logstash uses solely for Maven dependency resolution via jar-dependencies. The vulnerable org.codehaus.plexus.util.Expand.extractFile code path is never invoked: logstash performs all archive extraction using Ruby-native libraries (rubyzip, Gem::Package::TarReader), not Maven/plexus tooling.

GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9 affects tools.jackson.core/jackson-core 3.1.0 with no fixed version available. This JAR is bundled within the logstash-filter-elastic_integration plugin (logstash-filter-elastic_integration-9.3.2.jar) and is not directly controllable at the image definition level. Waiting for upstream Elastic plugin maintainers to update their jackson-core dependency and republish the plugin.

CVE-2026-33870 is a high-severity HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in Netty's chunked transfer encoding parser, fixed in 4.1.132.Final. Netty dependencies in the logstash image are bundled within upstream logstash plugins (logstash-input-http, logstash-input-beats, logstash-input-tcp) and are not directly controllable at the image definition level. Waiting for upstream Elastic plugin maintainers to update their netty dependencies.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.

Waiting for upstream logstash to update uri gem dependency to 0.12.4. CVE-2025-27221 affects uri gem 0.12.3 requiring upgrade to 0.12.4. However, Ruby gems in the logstash image are managed by the upstream logstash Gradle build process using installDefaultGems, not directly controllable at the image definition level. The logstash build installs gems from the official logstash repository's gem specifications, making gem version overrides dependent on upstream logstash changes.

Waiting for upstream logstash/JRuby to update bcpkix-jdk18on dependency to 1.79. CVE-2025-8916 affects org.bouncycastle/bcpkix-jdk18on 1.78 requiring upgrade to 1.79. However, BouncyCastle dependencies in the logstash image are part of the JRuby standard library bundled within the upstream logstash JRuby distribution. These JAR dependencies are managed by the upstream logstash Gradle build process and JRuby project, not directly controllable at the image definition level. Updates require upstream logstash and JRuby maintainers to update their BouncyCastle dependencies.

Fault injection based attacks are not within OpenSSLs threat model according to the security policy and this CVE is not treated as security bug by upstream: https://www.openssl.org/policies/general/security-policy.html

The only viable vector for exploitation of this bug is local, if a static setuid program exists, and that program calls dlopen, then it may search LD_LIBRARY_PATH to locate the SONAME to load. No such program is present in the container image .
